Providers that do not implement saveDiscoveryState at all keep\n    // the (legacy) warn-and-proceed behavior.\n    if (authorizationCode !== undefined) {\n        const recordedIssuer = cachedState?.authorizationServerMetadata?.issuer ?? cachedState?.authorizationServerUrl;\n        if (recordedIssuer === undefined) {\n            if (provider.saveDiscoveryState !== undefined) {\n                throw new AuthorizationServerMismatchError(\n                    'discoveryState was not available on the callback leg; ensure your provider persists discoveryState alongside codeVerifier',\n                    issuer\n                );\n            }\n            console.warn(\n                '[mcp-sdk] OAuthClientProvider does not implement saveDiscoveryState()/discoveryState(); ' +\n                    'the SEP-2352 callback-leg authorization-server binding cannot be checked. ' +\n                    'Implement discoveryState (persist alongside codeVerifier) — see docs/migration/upgrade-to-v2.md §SEP-2352.'\n            );\n        } else if (!issuersMatch(recordedIssuer, issuer)) {\n            throw new AuthorizationServerMismatchError(recordedIssuer, issuer);\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (freshDiscoveryState) {\n        await provider.saveDiscoveryState?.(freshDiscoveryState);\n    }\n\n    const resource: URL | undefined = await selectResourceURL(serverUrl, provider, resourceMetadata);\n\n    // Save resource URL for providers that need it (e.g., CrossAppAccessProvider)\n    if (resource) {\n        await provider.saveResourceUrl?.(String(resource));\n    }\n\n    // Scope selection used consistently for DCR and the authorization request.\n    const resolvedScope = determineScope({\n        requestedScope: scope,\n        resourceMetadata,\n        authServerMetadata: metadata,\n        clientMetadata: provider.clientMetadata\n    });\n\n    // Handle client registration if needed. SEP-2352: a stored credential whose `issuer`\n    // stamp names a different authorization server reads back as `undefined`, so the flow\n    // re-registers exactly as if nothing were stored.\n    const rawClientInfo = await Promise.resolve(provider.clientInformation(infoCtx));\n    let clientInformation = discardIfIssuerMismatch(rawClientInfo, issuer, {\n        canPersistStamp: provider.saveClientInformation !== undefined\n    });\n    if (clientInformation === undefined && rawClientInfo?.issuer && provider.saveClientInformation === undefined) {\n        // Static-credential provider (no DCR) whose `expectedIssuer` stamp names a different\n        // AS — surface the typed error with both issuers rather than the generic\n        // \"client information must be saveable for dynamic registration\" fallback.\n        throw new AuthorizationServerMismatchError(rawClientInfo.issuer, issuer);\n    }\n    if (clientInformation && clientInformation.issuer === undefined) {\n        // SEP-2352 back-stamp: legacy (pre-SEP-2352) storage returned an unstamped value.\n        // Bind it to the first AS resolved after upgrade so subsequent calls have a real\n        // stamp to compare against — closes the otherwise-permanent unstamped window.\n        clientInformation = { ...clientInformation, issuer };\n        await provider.saveClientInformation?.(clientInformation, infoCtx);\n    }\n    if (!clientInformation) {\n        if (authorizationCode !== undefined) {\n            throw new Error('Existing OAuth client information is required when exchanging an authorization code');\n        }\n\n        const supportsUrlBasedClientId = metadata?.client_id_metadata_document_supported === true;\n        const clientMetadataUrl = provider.clientMetadataUrl;\n\n        if (clientMetadataUrl && !isHttpsUrl(clientMetadataUrl)) {\n            throw new OAuthError(\n                OAuthErrorCode.InvalidClientMetadata,\n                `clientMetadataUrl must be a valid HTTPS URL with a non-root pathname, got: ${clientMetadataUrl}`\n            );\n        }\n\n        const shouldUseUrlBasedClientId = supportsUrlBasedClientId && clientMetadataUrl;\n\n        if (shouldUseUrlBasedClientId) {\n            // SEP-991: URL-based Client IDs\n            clientInformation = { client_id: clientMetadataUrl, issuer };\n            await provider.saveClientInformation?.(clientInformation, infoCtx);\n        } else {\n            // Fallback to dynamic registration\n            if (!provider.saveClientInformation) {\n                throw new Error('OAuth client information must be saveable for dynamic registration');\n            }\n\n            const fullInformation = await registerClient(authorizationServerUrl, {\n                metadata,\n                clientMetadata,\n                scope: resolvedScope,\n                fetchFn\n            });\n\n            clientInformation = { ...fullInformation, issuer };\n            await provider.saveClientInformation(clientInformation, infoCtx);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Non-interactive flows (e.g., client_credentials, jwt-bearer) don't need a redirect URL\n    const nonInteractiveFlow = !provider.redirectUrl;\n\n    // Exchange authorization code for tokens, or fetch tokens directly for non-interactive flows\n    if (authorizationCode !== undefined || nonInteractiveFlow) {\n        // RFC 9207: validate the callback `iss` against the recorded issuer before the\n        // authorization code is sent to any token endpoint. Non-interactive flows have no\n        // authorization response, so the gate is keyed on `authorizationCode`.\n        if (authorizationCode !== undefined) {\n            validateAuthorizationResponseIssuer({\n                iss,\n                expectedIssuer: metadata?.issuer,\n                issParameterSupported: isIssParameterSupported(metadata)\n            });\n        }\n\n        const tokens = await fetchToken(provider, authorizationServerUrl, {\n            metadata,\n            resource,\n            authorizationCode,\n            iss,\n            scope: resolvedScope,\n            fetchFn\n        });\n\n        await provider.saveTokens({ ...tokens, issuer }, infoCtx);\n        return 'AUTHORIZED';\n    }\n\n    // SEP-2352: a refresh_token stamped for a different authorization server reads back\n    // as `undefined`, so it is never POSTed to this AS's token endpoint.\n    let tokens = discardIfIssuerMismatch(await provider.tokens(infoCtx), issuer);\n    if (tokens && tokens.issuer === undefined) {\n        // SEP-2352 back-stamp: bind a legacy unstamped token set to the first-resolved AS\n        // so the stamp check is effective from the next call onward.\n        tokens = { ...tokens, issuer };\n        await provider.saveTokens(tokens, infoCtx);\n    }\n\n    // Handle token refresh or new authorization. The step-up path sets\n    // `forceReauthorization` when the requested scope strictly exceeds the\n    // current token's granted scope — refreshing would not widen it (RFC 6749\n    // §6), so skip straight to a fresh authorization request.\n    if (tokens?.refresh_token && !forceReauthorization) {\n        try {\n            // Attempt to refresh the token\n            const newTokens = await refreshAuthorization(authorizationServerUrl, {\n                metadata,\n                clientInformation,\n                refreshToken: tokens.refresh_token,\n                resource,\n                addClientAuthentication: provider.addClientAuthentication,\n                fetchFn\n            });\n\n            await provider.saveTokens({ ...newTokens, issuer }, infoCtx);\n            return 'AUTHORIZED';\n        } catch (error) {\n            // A non-TLS token endpoint is a configuration error — re-authorizing cannot\n            // fix it. Surface it so the consumer sees the misconfiguration instead of an\n            // unexplained re-auth prompt.\n            if (error instanceof InsecureTokenEndpointError) {\n                throw error;\n            }\n            // If this is a ServerError, or an unknown type, log it out and try to continue. Otherwise, escalate so we can fix things and retry.\n            if (!(error instanceof OAuthError) || error.code === OAuthErrorCode.ServerError) {\n                // Could not refresh OAuth tokens\n            } else {\n                // Refresh failed for another reason, re-throw\n                throw error;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    const state = provider.state ? await provider.state() : undefined;\n\n    // Start new authorization flow\n    const { authorizationUrl, codeVerifier } = await startAuthorization(authorizationServerUrl, {\n        metadata,\n        clientInformation,\n        state,\n        redirectUrl: provider.redirectUrl,\n        scope: resolvedScope,\n        resource\n    });\n\n    await provider.saveCodeVerifier(codeVerifier);\n    await provider.redirectToAuthorization(authorizationUrl);\n    return 'REDIRECT';\n}\n\n/**\n * Validates that the given `clientMetadataUrl` is a valid HTTPS URL with a non-root pathname.\n *\n * No-op when `url` is `undefined` or empty (providers that do not use URL-based client IDs\n * are unaffected). When the value is defined but invalid, throws an {@linkcode OAuthError}\n * with code {@linkcode OAuthErrorCode.InvalidClientMetadata}.\n *\n * {@linkcode OAuthClientProvider} implementations that accept a `clientMetadataUrl` should\n * call this in their constructors for early validation.\n *\n * @param url - The `clientMetadataUrl` value to validate (from `OAuthClientProvider.clientMetadataUrl`)\n * @throws {OAuthError} When `url` is defined but is not a valid HTTPS URL with a non-root pathname\n */\nexport function validateClientMetadataUrl(url: string | undefined): void {\n    if (url && !isHttpsUrl(url)) {\n        throw new OAuthError(\n            OAuthErrorCode.InvalidClientMetadata,\n            `clientMetadataUrl must be a valid HTTPS URL with a non-root pathname, got: ${url}`\n        );\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * SEP-991: URL-based Client IDs\n * Validate that the `client_id` is a valid URL with `https` scheme\n */\nexport function isHttpsUrl(value?: string): boolean {\n    if (!value) return false;\n    try {\n        const url = new URL(value);\n        return url.protocol === 'https:' && url.pathname !== '/';\n    } catch {\n        return false;\n    }\n}\n\nexport async function selectResourceURL(\n    serverUrl: string | URL,\n    provider: OAuthClientProvider,\n    resourceMetadata?: OAuthProtectedResourceMetadata\n): Promise<URL | undefined> {\n    const defaultResource = resourceUrlFromServerUrl(serverUrl);\n\n    // If provider has custom validation, delegate to it\n    if (provider.validateResourceURL) {\n        return await provider.validateResourceURL(defaultResource, resourceMetadata?.resource);\n    }\n\n    // Only include resource parameter when Protected Resource Metadata is present\n    if (!resourceMetadata) {\n        return undefined;\n    }\n\n    // Validate that the metadata's resource is compatible with our request\n    if (!checkResourceAllowed({ requestedResource: defaultResource, configuredResource: resourceMetadata.resource })) {\n        throw new Error(`Protected resource ${resourceMetadata.resource} does not match expected ${defaultResource} (or origin)`);\n    }\n    // Prefer the resource from metadata since it's what the server is telling us to request\n    return new URL(resourceMetadata.resource);\n}\n\n/**\n * Extract `resource_metadata`, `scope`, `error`, and `error_description` from a\n * `WWW-Authenticate` header.\n */\nexport function extractWWWAuthenticateParams(res: Response): {\n    resourceMetadataUrl?: URL;\n    scope?: string;\n    error?: string;\n    errorDescription?: string;\n} {\n    const authenticateHeader = res.headers.get('WWW-Authenticate');\n    if (!authenticateHeader) {\n        return {};\n    }\n\n    const [type, scheme] = authenticateHeader.split(' ');\n    if (type?.toLowerCase() !== 'bearer' || !scheme) {\n        return {};\n    }\n\n    const resourceMetadataMatch = extractFieldFromWwwAuth(res, 'resource_metadata') || undefined;\n\n    let resourceMetadataUrl: URL | undefined;\n    if (resourceMetadataMatch) {\n        try {\n            resourceMetadataUrl = new URL(resourceMetadataMatch);\n        } catch {\n            // Ignore invalid URL\n        }\n    }\n\n    const scope = extractFieldFromWwwAuth(res, 'scope') || undefined;\n    const error = extractFieldFromWwwAuth(res, 'error') || undefined;\n    const errorDescription = extractFieldFromWwwAuth(res, 'error_description') || undefined;\n\n    return {\n        resourceMetadataUrl,\n        scope,\n        error,\n        errorDescription\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Extracts a specific field's value from the `WWW-Authenticate` header string.\n *\n * @param response The HTTP response object containing the headers.\n * @param fieldName The name of the field to extract (e.g., `\"realm\"`, `\"nonce\"`).\n * @returns The field value\n */\nfunction extractFieldFromWwwAuth(response: Response, fieldName: string): string | null {\n    const wwwAuthHeader = response.headers.get('WWW-Authenticate');\n    if (!wwwAuthHeader) {\n        return null;\n    }\n\n    const pattern = new RegExp(String.raw`${fieldName}=(?:\"([^\"]+)\"|([^\\s,]+))`);\n    const match = wwwAuthHeader.match(pattern);\n\n    if (match) {\n        // Pattern matches: field_name=\"value\" or field_name=value (unquoted)\n        const result = match[1] || match[2];\n        if (result) {\n            return result;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return null;\n}\n\n/**\n * Extract `resource_metadata` from response header.\n * @deprecated Use {@linkcode extractWWWAuthenticateParams} instead.\n */\nexport function extractResourceMetadataUrl(res: Response): URL | undefined {\n    const authenticateHeader = res.headers.get('WWW-Authenticate');\n    if (!authenticateHeader) {\n        return undefined;\n    }\n\n    const [type, scheme] = authenticateHeader.split(' ');\n    if (type?.toLowerCase() !== 'bearer' || !scheme) {\n        return undefined;\n    }\n    const regex = /resource_metadata=\"([^\"]*)\"/;\n    const match = regex.exec(authenticateHeader);\n\n    if (!match || !match[1]) {\n        return undefined;\n    }\n\n    try {\n        return new URL(match[1]);\n    } catch {\n        return undefined;\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Looks up {@link https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9728 | RFC 9728}\n * OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata.\n *\n * If the server returns a 404 for the well-known endpoint, this function will\n * return `undefined`. Any other errors will be thrown as exceptions.\n */\nexport async function discoverOAuthProtectedResourceMetadata(\n    serverUrl: string | URL,\n    opts?: { protocolVersion?: string; resourceMetadataUrl?: string | URL },\n    fetchFn: FetchLike = fetch\n): Promise<OAuthProtectedResourceMetadata> {\n    const response = await discoverMetadataWithFallback(serverUrl, 'oauth-protected-resource', fetchFn, {\n        protocolVersion: opts?.protocolVersion,\n        metadataUrl: opts?.resourceMetadataUrl\n    });\n\n    if (!response || response.status === 404) {\n        await response?.text?.().catch(() => {});\n        throw new Error(`Resource server does not implement OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata.`);\n    }\n\n    if (!response.ok) {\n        await response.text?.().catch(() => {});\n        throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status} trying to load well-known OAuth protected resource metadata.`);\n    }\n    return OAuthProtectedResourceMetadataSchema.parse(await response.json());\n}\n\n/**\n * Fetch with a retry heuristic for CORS errors caused by custom headers.\n *\n * In browsers, adding a custom header (e.g. `MCP-Protocol-Version`) triggers a CORS preflight.\n * If the server doesn't allow that header, the browser throws a `TypeError` before any response\n * is received. Retrying without custom headers often succeeds because the request becomes\n * \"simple\" (no preflight). If the server sends no CORS headers at all, the retry also fails\n * with `TypeError` and we return `undefined` so callers can fall through to an alternate URL.\n *\n * However, `fetch()` also throws `TypeError` for non-CORS failures (DNS resolution, connection\n * refused, invalid URL). Swallowing those and returning `undefined` masks real errors and can\n * cause callers to silently fall through to a different discovery URL. CORS is a browser-only\n * concept, so in non-browser runtimes (Node.js, Workers) a `TypeError` from `fetch` is never a\n * CORS error — there we propagate the error instead of swallowing it.\n *\n * In browsers, we cannot reliably distinguish CORS `TypeError` from network `TypeError` from the\n * error object alone, so the swallow-and-fallthrough heuristic is preserved there.\n */\nasync function fetchWithCorsRetry(url: URL, headers?: Record<string, string>, fetchFn: FetchLike = fetch): Promise<Response | undefined> {\n    try {\n        return await fetchFn(url, { headers });\n    } catch (error) {\n        if (!(error instanceof TypeError) || !CORS_IS_POSSIBLE) {\n            throw error;\n        }\n        if (headers) {\n            // Could be a CORS preflight rejection caused by our custom header. Retry as a simple\n            // request: if that succeeds, we've sidestepped the preflight.\n            try {\n                return await fetchFn(url, {});\n            } catch (retryError) {\n                if (!(retryError instanceof TypeError)) {\n                    throw retryError;\n                }\n                // Retry also got CORS-blocked (server sends no CORS headers at all).\n                // Return undefined so the caller tries the next discovery URL.\n                return undefined;\n            }\n        }\n        return undefined;\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Constructs the well-known path for auth-related metadata discovery\n */\nfunction buildWellKnownPath(\n    wellKnownPrefix: 'oauth-authorization-server' | 'oauth-protected-resource' | 'openid-configuration',\n    pathname: string = '',\n    options: { prependPathname?: boolean } = {}\n): string {\n    // Strip trailing slash from pathname to avoid double slashes\n    if (pathname.endsWith('/')) {\n        pathname = pathname.slice(0, -1);\n    }\n\n    return options.prependPathname ? `${pathname}/.well-known/${wellKnownPrefix}` : `/.well-known/${wellKnownPrefix}${pathname}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Tries to discover OAuth metadata at a specific URL\n */\nasync function tryMetadataDiscovery(url: URL, protocolVersion: string, fetchFn: FetchLike = fetch): Promise<Response | undefined> {\n    const headers = {\n        'MCP-Protocol-Version': protocolVersion\n    };\n    return await fetchWithCorsRetry(url, headers, fetchFn);\n}\n\n/**\n * Determines if fallback to root discovery should be attempted\n */\nfunction shouldAttemptFallback(response: Response | undefined, pathname: string): boolean {\n    if (!response) return true; // CORS error — always try fallback\n    if (pathname === '/') return false; // Already at root\n    return (response.status >= 400 && response.status < 500) || response.status === 502;\n}\n\n/**\n * Generic function for discovering OAuth metadata with fallback support\n */\nasync function discoverMetadataWithFallback(\n    serverUrl: string | URL,\n    wellKnownType: 'oauth-authorization-server' | 'oauth-protected-resource',\n    fetchFn: FetchLike,\n    opts?: { protocolVersion?: string; metadataUrl?: string | URL; metadataServerUrl?: string | URL }\n): Promise<Response | undefined> {\n    const issuer = new URL(serverUrl);\n    const protocolVersion = opts?.protocolVersion ?? LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION;\n\n    let url: URL;\n    if (opts?.metadataUrl) {\n        url = new URL(opts.metadataUrl);\n    } else {\n        // Try path-aware discovery first\n        const wellKnownPath = buildWellKnownPath(wellKnownType, issuer.pathname);\n        url = new URL(wellKnownPath, opts?.metadataServerUrl ?? issuer);\n        url.search = issuer.search;\n    }\n\n    let response = await tryMetadataDiscovery(url, protocolVersion, fetchFn);\n\n    // If path-aware discovery fails (4xx or 502 Bad Gateway) and we're not already at root, try fallback to root discovery\n    if (!opts?.metadataUrl && shouldAttemptFallback(response, issuer.pathname)) {\n        const rootUrl = new URL(`/.well-known/${wellKnownType}`, issuer);\n        response = await tryMetadataDiscovery(rootUrl, protocolVersion, fetchFn);\n    }\n\n    return response;\n}\n\n/**\n * Looks up RFC 8414 OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata.\n *\n * If the server returns a 404 for the well-known endpoint, this function will\n * return `undefined`. Any other errors will be thrown as exceptions.\n *\n * @deprecated This function is deprecated in favor of {@linkcode discoverAuthorizationServerMetadata}.\n */\nexport async function discoverOAuthMetadata(\n    issuer: string | URL,\n    {\n        authorizationServerUrl,\n        protocolVersion\n    }: {\n        authorizationServerUrl?: string | URL;\n        protocolVersion?: string;\n    } = {},\n    fetchFn: FetchLike = fetch\n): Promise<OAuthMetadata | undefined> {\n    if (typeof issuer === 'string') {\n        issuer = new URL(issuer);\n    }\n    if (!authorizationServerUrl) {\n        authorizationServerUrl = issuer;\n    }\n    if (typeof authorizationServerUrl === 'string') {\n        authorizationServerUrl = new URL(authorizationServerUrl);\n    }\n    protocolVersion ??= LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION;\n\n    const response = await discoverMetadataWithFallback(authorizationServerUrl, 'oauth-authorization-server', fetchFn, {\n        protocolVersion,\n        metadataServerUrl: authorizationServerUrl\n    });\n\n    if (!response || response.status === 404) {\n        await response?.text?.().catch(() => {});\n        return undefined;\n    }\n\n    if (!response.ok) {\n        await response.text?.().catch(() => {});\n        throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status} trying to load well-known OAuth metadata`);\n    }\n\n    return OAuthMetadataSchema.parse(await response.json());\n}\n\n/**\n * Builds a list of discovery URLs to try for authorization server metadata.\n * URLs are returned in priority order:\n * 1. OAuth metadata at the given URL\n * 2. OIDC metadata endpoints at the given URL\n */\nexport function buildDiscoveryUrls(authorizationServerUrl: string | URL): { url: URL; type: 'oauth' | 'oidc' }[] {\n    const url = typeof authorizationServerUrl === 'string' ? new URL(authorizationServerUrl) : authorizationServerUrl;\n    const hasPath = url.pathname !== '/';\n    const urlsToTry: { url: URL; type: 'oauth' | 'oidc' }[] = [];\n\n    if (!hasPath) {\n        urlsToTry.push(\n            // Root path: https://example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server\n\n            {\n                url: new URL('/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server', url.origin),\n                type: 'oauth'\n            },\n            // OIDC: https://example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration\n\n            {\n                url: new URL(`/.well-known/openid-configuration`, url.origin),\n                type: 'oidc'\n            }\n        );\n\n        return urlsToTry;\n    }\n\n    // Strip trailing slash from pathname to avoid double slashes\n    let pathname = url.pathname;\n    if (pathname.endsWith('/')) {\n        pathname = pathname.slice(0, -1);\n    }\n\n    urlsToTry.push(\n        // 1. OAuth metadata at the given URL\n        // Insert well-known before the path: https://example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/tenant1\n        {\n            url: new URL(`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server${pathname}`, url.origin),\n            type: 'oauth'\n        },\n        // 2. OIDC metadata endpoints\n        // RFC 8414 style: Insert /.well-known/openid-configuration before the path\n        {\n            url: new URL(`/.well-known/openid-configuration${pathname}`, url.origin),\n            type: 'oidc'\n        },\n        // OIDC Discovery 1.0 style: Append /.well-known/openid-configuration after the path\n\n        {\n            url: new URL(`${pathname}/.well-known/openid-configuration`, url.origin),\n            type: 'oidc'\n        }\n    );\n\n    return urlsToTry;\n}\n\n/**\n * Discovers authorization server metadata with support for\n * {@link https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8414 | RFC 8414} OAuth 2.0\n * Authorization Server Metadata and\n * {@link https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-discovery-1_0.html | OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0}\n * specifications.\n *\n * This function implements a fallback strategy for authorization server discovery:\n * 1. Attempts RFC 8414 OAuth metadata discovery first\n * 2. If OAuth discovery fails, falls back to OpenID Connect Discovery\n *\n * @param authorizationServerUrl - The authorization server URL obtained from the MCP Server's\n *                                 protected resource metadata, or the MCP server's URL if the\n *                                 metadata was not found.\n * The returned metadata's `issuer` is validated against `authorizationServerUrl`\n * per RFC 8414 §3.3 (and OIDC Discovery §4.3): if they differ the metadata is\n * **rejected** with {@linkcode IssuerMismatchError} and not returned. Set\n * `skipIssuerValidation: true` to suppress this check — **security-weakening**,\n * intended only for known-misconfigured authorization servers.\n *\n * @param options - Configuration options\n * @param options.fetchFn - Optional fetch function for making HTTP requests, defaults to global fetch\n * @param options.protocolVersion - MCP protocol version to use, defaults to {@linkcode LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION}\n * @param options.skipIssuerValidation - Skip the RFC 8414 §3.3 `issuer` echo check. **Security-weakening.**\n * @returns Promise resolving to authorization server metadata, or undefined if discovery fails\n * @throws {IssuerMismatchError} when the metadata's `issuer` does not match `authorizationServerUrl`\n */\nexport async function discoverAuthorizationServerMetadata(\n    authorizationServerUrl: string | URL,\n    {\n        fetchFn = fetch,\n        protocolVersion = LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION,\n        skipIssuerValidation = false\n    }: {\n        fetchFn?: FetchLike;\n        protocolVersion?: string;\n        skipIssuerValidation?: boolean;\n    } = {}\n): Promise<AuthorizationServerMetadata | undefined> {\n    const headers = {\n        'MCP-Protocol-Version': protocolVersion,\n        Accept: 'application/json'\n    };\n\n    // Get the list of URLs to try\n    const urlsToTry = buildDiscoveryUrls(authorizationServerUrl);\n\n    // Try each URL in order\n    for (const { url: endpointUrl, type } of urlsToTry) {\n        const response = await fetchWithCorsRetry(endpointUrl, headers, fetchFn);\n\n        if (!response) {\n            /**\n             * CORS error occurred - don't throw as the endpoint may not allow CORS,\n             * continue trying other possible endpoints\n             */\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        if (!response.ok) {\n            await response.text?.().catch(() => {});\n            if ((response.status >= 400 && response.status < 500) || response.status === 502) {\n                continue; // Try next URL for 4xx or 502 (Bad Gateway)\n            }\n            throw new Error(\n                `HTTP ${response.status} trying to load ${type === 'oauth' ? 'OAuth' : 'OpenID provider'} metadata from ${endpointUrl}`\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Parse and validate based on type\n        const parsed =\n            type === 'oauth'\n                ? OAuthMetadataSchema.parse(await response.json())\n                : OpenIdProviderDiscoveryMetadataSchema.parse(await response.json());\n\n        if (!skipIssuerValidation) {\n            // RFC 8414 §3.3 / OIDC Discovery §4.3: the `issuer` value in the document MUST be\n            // identical to the issuer identifier used to construct the well-known URL. Compare\n            // against the raw input string — callers pass the exact issuer string the AS published.\n            const expectedIssuer = typeof authorizationServerUrl === 'string' ? authorizationServerUrl : authorizationServerUrl.href;\n            // One narrow tolerance: the SDK's own legacy-fallback path synthesizes the AS URL via\n            // `String(new URL('/', serverUrl))`, which always carries a trailing `/`. That value is\n            // SDK-generated (not attacker-controlled), so accept the slash-only difference here.\n            // The tolerance is one-directional and end-anchored — a different host or path is still\n            // a mismatch.\n            const matches =\n                parsed.issuer === expectedIssuer || (expectedIssuer.endsWith('/') && parsed.issuer === expectedIssuer.slice(0, -1));\n            if (!matches) {\n                throw new IssuerMismatchError('metadata', expectedIssuer, parsed.issuer);\n            }\n        }\n\n        return parsed;\n    }\n\n    return undefined;\n}\n\n/**\n * Result of {@linkcode discoverOAuthServerInfo}.\n */\nexport interface OAuthServerInfo {\n    /**\n     * The authorization server URL, either discovered via RFC 9728\n     * or derived from the MCP server URL as a fallback.\n     */\n    authorizationServerUrl: string;\n\n    /**\n     * The authorization server metadata (endpoints, capabilities),\n     * or `undefined` if metadata discovery failed.\n     */\n    authorizationServerMetadata?: AuthorizationServerMetadata;\n\n    /**\n     * The OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata from RFC 9728,\n     * or `undefined` if the server does not support it.\n     */\n    resourceMetadata?: OAuthProtectedResourceMetadata;\n}\n\n/**\n * Discovers the authorization server for an MCP server following\n * {@link https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9728 | RFC 9728} (OAuth 2.0 Protected\n * Resource Metadata), with fallback to treating the server URL as the\n * authorization server.\n *\n * This function combines two discovery steps into one call:\n * 1. createPrivateKeyJwtAuth(options: {\n    issuer: string;\n    subject: string;\n    privateKey: string | Uint8Array | Record<string, unknown>;\n    alg: string;\n    audience?: string | URL;\n    lifetimeSeconds?: number;\n    claims?: Record<string, unknown>;\n}): AddClientAuthentication {\n    return async (_headers, params, url, metadata) => {\n        // Lazy import to avoid heavy The `tools/list`-derived index (mirroring / output\n *   validation) is therefore unaffected by a `'bypass'` call.\n */\nexport type CacheMode = 'use' | 'refresh' | 'bypass';\n\n/**\n * A logical cache address. `params` is the canonical result-affecting params\n * key (`''` for the four list ops, the `uri` for `resources/read`); omitted is\n * equivalent to `''`. `partition` namespaces the entry by connected-server\n * identity AND per-principal scope: the `Client` writes a JSON-encoded\n * `[serverIdentity, principal]` pair (so a server-controlled `serverInfo`\n * string cannot bleed into the principal slot regardless of what characters\n * it contains). When inserting a new `resources/read` key\n     * would exceed this, the oldest such entry (by insertion order) is\n     * evicted first. The list-singleton methods (`tools/list`,\n     * `prompts/list`, `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list`,\n     * `server/discover`) are **exempt** — they hold at most one entry per\n     * partition and back the `tools/list`-derived index, so an unbounded URI\n     * working set never displaces them. The default of `512` bounds growth on\n     * a long-lived client against template-expanded URIs. `0` disables the\n     * bound.\n     */\n    maxEntries?: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Methods whose entries are exempt from the\n * {@linkcode InMemoryResponseCacheStoreOptions.maxEntries} cap. Each holds at\n * most one entry per partition (a small bounded set) and the\n * `tools/list`-derived index depends on its entry surviving regardless of the\n * `resources/read` working-set size. the list-singleton methods are exempt and never\n * evicted by the cap. `Map` preserves insertion order, so the oldest live\n * capped key is the first matching iteration entry.\n */\nexport class InMemoryResponseCacheStore implements ResponseCacheStore {\n    private readonly _entries = new Map<string, CacheEntry>();\n    private readonly _maxEntries: number;\n    private _stamp = 0;\n    /** Count of held entries that are subject to the cap (i.e. not in {@linkcode CAP_EXEMPT_METHODS}). */\n    private _cappedSize = 0;\n\n    constructor(options?: InMemoryResponseCacheStoreOptions) {\n        this._maxEntries = options?.maxEntries ?? 512;\n    }\n\n    /** Number of held entries (for diagnostics / bounding tests). */\n    get size(): number {\n        return this._entries.size;\n    }\n\n    get(key: CacheKey): CacheEntry | undefined {\n        return this._entries.get(keyOf(key));\n    }\n\n    set(key: CacheKey, entry: { value: string; expiresAt?: number; scope?: CacheScope }): number {\n        const k = keyOf(key);\n        const exempt = CAP_EXEMPT_METHODS.has(key.method);\n        const isNew = !this._entries.has(k);\n        // Evict the oldest CAPPED entry first when adding a NEW capped key\n        // would exceed the cap (re-set of an existing key never evicts; an\n        // exempt-method write never evicts). `Map` iteration order is\n        // insertion order, so the first non-exempt key is the oldest one.\n        if (!exempt && isNew && this._maxEntries > 0 && this._cappedSize >= this._maxEntries) {\n            for (const oldKey of this._entries.keys()) {\n                if (!CAP_EXEMPT_METHODS.has(oldKey.slice(0, oldKey.indexOf('\\0')))) {\n                    this._entries.delete(oldKey);\n                    this._cappedSize--;\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        const stamp = ++this._stamp;\n        this._entries.set(k, { ...entry, stamp });\n        if (isNew && !exempt) this._cappedSize++;\n        return stamp;\n    }\n\n    delete(key: CacheKey): void {\n        if (this._entries.delete(keyOf(key)) && !CAP_EXEMPT_METHODS.has(key.method)) this._cappedSize--;\n    }\n\n    evict(method: string): void {\n        const prefix = `${method}\\0`;\n        const exempt = CAP_EXEMPT_METHODS.has(method);\n        for (const k of this._entries.keys()) {\n            if (k.startsWith(prefix)) {\n                this._entries.delete(k);\n                if (!exempt) this._cappedSize--;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    clear(): void {\n        this._entries.clear();\n        this._cappedSize = 0;\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Serialize a {@linkcode CacheKey} for the in-memory map. `method` is always\n * an SDK-set MCP method string (never contains a NUL), so the `\\0` prefix\n * delimiter is safe and lets {@linkcode InMemoryResponseCacheStore.evict} do a\n * cheap prefix scan. `partition` (already a JSON-encoded\n * `[serverIdentity, principal]` pair) and `params` (a resource URI on the\n * `resources/read` path — caller-controlled) are JSON-array-encoded together,\n * which is collision-free regardless of any NUL or delimiter characters they\n * carry.\n */\nfunction keyOf(key: CacheKey): string {\n    return `${key.method}\\0${JSON.stringify([key.partition ?? '', key.params ?? ''])}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Serialize a `{method, params}` pair for the eviction-generation map. The\n * list singletons key on `method` alone (their {@linkcode ClientResponseCache.evict}\n * is whole-method); `resources/read` keys on `` `${method}\\0${uri}` `` so\n * {@linkcode ClientResponseCache.evictKey} bumps a per-URI counter.\n */\nfunction genKey(method: string, params?: string): string {\n    return params === undefined ? method : `${method}\\0${params}`;\n}\n\n/**\n * Upper bound on the server-supplied `ttlMs` honoured by\n * {@linkcode ClientResponseCache} (24h). A server cannot pin an entry\n * indefinitely.\n */\nexport const MAX_CACHE_TTL_MS = 86_400_000;\n\n/**\n * The `Client`'s cache-coordination collaborator.\n *\n * Owns the per-connection cache state that used to live as five private\n * fields on `Client` — the backing {@linkcode ResponseCacheStore}, the\n * per-method eviction-generation counter, the user-supplied/default flag, and\n * the stamp-memoized derived indices over the `tools/list` entry. `Client`\n * holds exactly one instance and never reaches past it to the store.\n *\n * Not exported from the package index — internal to the client package.\n *\n * @internal\n */\nexport class ClientResponseCache {\n    /**\n     * Per-logical-key eviction-generation counter. {@linkcode evict} (whole\n     * method) and {@linkcode evictKey} (single `{method, params}`) bump it\n     * before touching the store; {@linkcode captureGeneration} reads it before\n     * the request; {@linkcode write} skips when it moved — so a `list_changed`\n     * arriving mid-walk, or a `resources/updated` arriving while a\n     * `readResource()` for the same URI is in flight, is not overwritten by\n     * the in-flight request's stale write. The\n         * `Client` wires this to `onerror`.\n         */\n        private readonly _reportError: (error: unknown) => void = () => {},\n        /**\n         * The opaque per-principal identifier for this client (the\n         * `private`-scope storage slot within the connected server's\n         * namespace). `''` (the default) makes the `private` slot identical to\n         * the server's shared `public` slot — the safe single-tenant posture.\n         * See `_partitionFor`.\n         */\n        private readonly _cachePartition: string = '',\n        /**\n         * Clock seam (testing). The freshness check (`entry.expiresAt > now()`)\n         * and the `expiresAt = now() + ttlMs` stamp both read it via\n         * {@linkcode now}. Surrogate-keyed\n     * partitions are NOT stable across reconnects — no identity means no\n     * cross-connection cache reuse, and a shared long-lived store should\n     * bound its own size accordingly. Every partition derived after this\n     * call is scoped to this identity; entries written under the pre-connect\n     * `''` sentinel are no longer reachable.\n     */\n    setServerIdentity(identity: string): void {\n        this._serverIdentity = identity;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Derive the storage partition for `scope`. The encoding is\n     * `JSON.stringify([serverIdentity, principal])` — JSON escaping makes it\n     * collision-free by construction: a malicious server cannot craft a\n     * `serverInfo.name`/`version` whose concatenated form bleeds into another\n     * server's namespace or another principal's slot, regardless of `@` / `|`\n     * / `\"` / NUL in the server-controlled strings. `'public'` →\n     * `[serverIdentity, '']` (shared within this server); `'private'` →\n     * `[serverIdentity, cachePartition]`. '' : this._cachePartition]);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Two-probe lookup: this client's own (private) partition first, then the\n     * connected server's shared (public) partition. The shared probe is gated\n     * on `entry.scope === 'public'` — a co-tenant client that omits\n     * `cachePartition` writes its `'private'`-scoped entries at the public\n     * partition, and serving those to a correctly-partitioned client would\n     * leak private bodies (mcp.d's `cachedEntry` two-probe order; the scope\n     * gate is defence-in-depth on top of the partition split). When\n     * `cachePartition` is `''` the two partitions are identical and only one\n     * probe is issued.\n     */\n    private async _probe(method: string, params?: string): Promise<CacheEntry | undefined> {\n        const key = { method, params: params ?? '' };\n        const ownPartition = this._partitionFor('private');\n        const own = await this._store.get({ ...key, partition: ownPartition });\n        if (own !== undefined) return own;\n        const sharedPartition = this._partitionFor('public');\n        if (sharedPartition === ownPartition) return undefined;\n        const shared = await this._store.get({ ...key, partition: sharedPartition });\n        return shared?.scope === 'public' ? shared : undefined;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Bump the per-method generation (so an in-flight {@linkcode write} for the\n     * same method becomes a no-op) and drop the connected server's two list\n     * singletons (own + shared partition; `params: ''`). The generation bump\n     * is unconditional and FIRST — the {@linkcode write} race guard relies on\n     * the bump, not on the store's deletes completing.\n     *\n     * Eviction is scoped to this client's `[serverIdentity, principal]`\n     * partitions (mirroring {@linkcode evictKey}) — the method-wide\n     * `store.evict()` is NOT called, so on a shared store one server's\n     * `list_changed` cannot wipe a co-tenant's entry. A custom store's\n     * `delete()` may throw or reject; each partition is guarded\n     * independently so a failure on one does not skip the other, the failure\n     * is reported via the constructor's sink, and the call resolves so\n     * dispatch proceeds.\n     */\n    async evict(method: string): Promise<void> {\n        this._evictionGeneration.set(method, (this._evictionGeneration.get(method) ?? 0) + 1);\n        await this._deleteBoth(method, '');\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Guarded two-partition delete of `{method, params}`: each partition's\n     * `delete` is independently wrapped so a custom store's failure on one is\n     * reported and does not skip the other, and the call always resolves.\n     */\n    private async _deleteBoth(method: string, params: string): Promise<void> {\n        const ownPartition = this._partitionFor('private');\n        const sharedPartition = this._partitionFor('public');\n        try {\n            await this._store.delete({ method, params, partition: ownPartition });\n        } catch (error) {\n            this._reportError(error);\n        }\n        if (sharedPartition !== ownPartition) {\n            try {\n                await this._store.delete({ method, params, partition: sharedPartition });\n            } catch (error) {\n                this._reportError(error);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Drop the single logical entry `{method, params}` from BOTH the private\n     * and public partitions for this client's connected server (mcp.d's\n     * `invalidateLogical`). Used for `notifications/resources/updated`'s\n     * per-URI eviction. The per-key generation is bumped FIRST (so an\n     * in-flight {@linkcode write} for the same `{method, params}` becomes a\n     * no-op and cannot re-cache the now-stale body) but only when the key was\n     * already recorded by {@linkcode captureGeneration} — bounding the map to\n     * keys the client has actually read. A custom store's `delete()` may\n     * throw or reject; each partition's delete is guarded independently so a\n     * failure on one does not skip the other, and the call resolves so\n     * dispatch proceeds.\n     */\n    async evictKey(method: string, params: string): Promise<void> {\n        const gk = genKey(method, params);\n        // Only bump a key the client has actually captured: if no entry is\n        // present there is no in-flight write to suppress, and an\n        // unconditional bump would let a server streaming distinct-URI\n        // `resources/updated` notifications grow this map without bound. The\n        // store deletes still run regardless (a previously-written entry may\n        // be held even when the generation entry has since been cleared by\n        // `resetForReconnect`).\n        const current = this._evictionGeneration.get(gk);\n        if (current !== undefined) this._evictionGeneration.set(gk, current + 1);\n        await this._deleteBoth(method, params);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Snapshot the eviction generation for `{method, params}` before issuing\n     * the request (a list walk's page 1, or a `resources/read` for `params`).\n     * Records the key so an interleaved {@linkcode evictKey} for the same\n     * `{method, params}` knows there is an in-flight write to suppress and\n     * bumps; without the record, `evictKey`'s recorded-only bump would skip\n     * and the stale body would be cached.\n     */\n    captureGeneration(method: string, params?: string): number {\n        const gk = genKey(method, params);\n        const current = this._evictionGeneration.get(gk) ?? 0;\n        this._evictionGeneration.set(gk, current);\n        return current;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Write `value` under `{method}` unless the per-method generation moved\n     * since `capturedGen` was taken — a `list_changed` that landed mid-walk has\n     * already invalidated the result the caller is about to write, and\n     * overwriting the eviction with the stale aggregate would lose the\n     * invalidation.\n     *\n     * The value is stored as its JSON-serialized document; serialization\n     * doubles as the mutation barrier, so a caller mutating the returned\n     * aggregate cannot reach the cache or its derived indices. A value that\n     * is not JSON-serializable (reachable only via in-process transports)\n     * fails the write loudly into the `reportError` sink. A custom store\n     * whose `set()` throws or rejects is routed to the same sink and the\n     * write resolves — cache bookkeeping never costs the caller a result it\n     * already fetched.\n     *\n     * `freshness` carries the client-computed `expiresAt` (absolute ms epoch,\n     * `now + ttlMs`) and the server-reported `cacheScope`. The storage\n     * `partition` is derived from the scope via `_partitionFor`:\n     * `'public'` → `[serverIdentity, '']` (shared within this server);\n     * `'private'` → `[serverIdentity, cachePartition]` (so a shared store\n     * never serves a private entry to another identity). Absent `freshness`\n     * preserves the substrate write (no `expiresAt`, private partition) — the\n     * `tools/list` retain-for-schema posture: never served by\n     * {@linkcode read}'s freshness gate, always readable by\n     * {@linkcode toolDefinition}.\n     *\n     * After storing under the derived partition, the same `{method, params}`\n     * is deleted from the OPPOSITE partition (mirroring {@linkcode evictKey}'s\n     * two-partition posture). A server that flips a result's `cacheScope` for\n     * the same key would otherwise leave the previous entry in the other slot\n     * — and since `_probe` checks own-partition first, a stale private entry\n     * would shadow the fresh public one (or a stale public entry would keep\n     * serving co-tenants). Both store calls are independently guarded so a\n     * custom store's failure on one does not skip the other.\n     */\n    async write(\n        method: string,\n        value: unknown,\n        capturedGen: number,\n        freshness?: { expiresAt: number; scope: CacheScope; params?: string }\n    ): Promise<void> {\n        if ((this._evictionGeneration.get(genKey(method, freshness?.params)) ?? 0) !== capturedGen) return;\n        const params = freshness?.params ?? '';\n        const ownPartition = this._partitionFor('private');\n        const sharedPartition = this._partitionFor('public');\n        const partition = (freshness?.scope ?? 'private') === 'public' ? sharedPartition : ownPartition;\n        try {\n            await this._store.set(\n                { method, params, partition },\n                { value: encodeCacheValue(value), expiresAt: freshness?.expiresAt, scope: freshness?.scope }\n            );\n        } catch (error) {\n            this._reportError(error);\n        }\n        if (sharedPartition !== ownPartition) {\n            try {\n                await this._store.delete({\n                    method,\n                    params,\n                    partition: partition === ownPartition ? sharedPartition : ownPartition\n                });\n            } catch (error) {\n                this._reportError(error);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Serve the fresh cached result for `{method, params}`, or `undefined`.\n     * Lookup is the two-probe order (own-partition then this server's shared\n     * partition, gated on `scope === 'public'`); freshness is\n     * `entry.expiresAt > now()` (a missing `expiresAt` is never fresh),\n     * checked BEFORE decoding so stale entries cost no parse. Every hit is\n     * freshly parsed, so the caller owns the value outright. An entry whose\n     * document does not parse or is not an object (corrupted external\n     * store) is reported,\n     * deleted, and treated as a miss — deleted because a fresh-but-corrupt\n     * entry would otherwise re-parse and re-report on every read until its\n     * `expiresAt` passes.\n     */\n    async read(method: string, params?: string): Promise<{ value: unknown } | undefined> {\n        const entry = await this._probe(method, params);\n        if (entry?.expiresAt === undefined || !(entry.expiresAt > this.now())) return undefined;\n        try {\n            const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(entry.value);\n            if (typeof parsed !== 'object' || parsed === null || Array.isArray(parsed)) {\n                throw new TypeError('cached document is not an object');\n            }\n            return { value: parsed };\n        } catch (error) {\n            this._reportError(error);\n            await this._deleteBoth(method, params ?? '');\n            return undefined;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Connection reset. The per-instance default store IS cleared\n     * (connection-scoped); a user-supplied store is NOT — that would defeat\n     * the only reason to supply one. The generation map and every derived\n     * index are dropped regardless: they are connection-scoped even when the\n     * backing store survives, so the next read re-derives from whatever the\n     * store still holds.     return undefined;\n        }\n        if (this._toolIndex?.stamp !== entry.stamp) {\n            const list = this._decodeListTools(entry);\n            const byName = new Map<string, Tool>();\n   }\n        return this._toolIndex.byName.get(name);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * The compiled output-schema validator for tool `name`, derived from the\n     * cached `tools/list` entry — same source Consulted for the timeout and closed\n * rows: a stdio probe that times out — or whose child exits, closing the\n * connection — signals a legacy server, while an HTTP timeout or close stays\n * a typed error. Anything that is not the stdio child-process transport is\n * treated like HTTP.\n */\nexport type ProbeTransportKind = 'stdio' | 'http';\n\n/**\n * A normalized probe outcome, produced by the connect-time wiring from the raw\n * transport exchange.\n */\nexport type ProbeOutcome =\n    | { kind: 'result'; result: unknown }\n    /** Answered with a JSON-RPC error (any HTTP status, including 200-bodied errors and stdio in-band errors). */\n    | { kind: 'rpc-error'; code: number; message: string; data?: unknown }\n    /** The HTTP layer rejected the probe POST (non-2xx); `body` is the raw response text and `statusText` the HTTP reason phrase, when available. */\n    | { kind: 'http-error'; status: number; body?: string; statusText?: string }\n    | { kind: 'network-error'; error: unknown }\n    /** The transport's auth flow challenged or failed during the probe send — an error stamped at a transport auth seam, or an `UnauthorizedError` (the foreign-transport contract). `error` propagates unchanged. */\n    | { kind: 'auth-required'; error: Error }\n    /** The transport reported close while the probe awaited its reply. */\n    | { kind: 'closed' }\n    /** No response arrived within the probe timeout. */\n    | { kind: 'timeout'; timeoutMs: number };\n\nexport interface ProbeClassifierContext {\n    /** Modern-era versions this client can negotiate, in preference order (never empty). */\n    clientModernVersions: readonly string[];\n    /** The version the probe carried in its `_meta` envelope (used to synthesize `data.requested` on typed errors). */\n    requestedVersion: string;\n    /**\n     * Whether a legacy `initialize` fallback is possible — `false` for a\n     * modern-only client and for `pin` mode. Without a fallback, rows carrying\n     * modern evidence but no usable version overlap — a `DiscoverResult` with\n     * no overlapping version, or a `-32022` whose `data.supported` lists only\n     * legacy revisions — yield a typed `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` built\n     * from that evidence; the remaining rows that would have fallen back still\n     * classify as `legacy`, and the caller reports them as a typed negotiation\n     * error instead of starting an `initialize` handshake.\n     */\n    fallbackAvailable: boolean;\n    /** See {@linkcode ProbeEnvironment}. */\n    environment: ProbeEnvironment;\n    /** See {@linkcode ProbeTransportKind}. */\n    transportKind: ProbeTransportKind;\n}\n\nexport type ProbeVerdict =\n    /** Definitive modern evidence: select `version` and continue without `initialize`. */\n    | { kind: 'modern'; version: string; discover: DiscoverResult }\n    /**\n     * `-32022` with a mutual modern version: re-send the probe at `version`.\n     * Spec-mandated select-and-continue — the caller runs it exactly once and\n     * arms a loop guard on the second rejection, throwing `error`.\n     */\n    | { kind: 'corrective'; version: string; error: UnsupportedProtocolVersionError }\n    /** Definitive legacy signal or unrecognized shape: perform the plain legacy `initialize` handshake (on the probed connection in the in-place modes; on the session child's fresh pipe on the sibling path). */\n    | { kind: 'legacy' }\n    /** Typed connect error — never converted to an era verdict. */\n    | { kind: 'error'; error: Error };\n\n/**\n * A cached era verdict for `connect({ prior })` — the persistable subset of\n * the {@linkcode ProbeVerdict} vocabulary (`'modern'` = speaks 2026-07-28+,\n * `'legacy'` = 2025-era `initialize` only). Freshness is the supplying host's\n * responsibility: a stale modern verdict fails loudly at the first request,\n * but a stale legacy verdict succeeds silently forever (an upgraded server\n * still answers `initialize`) — date cached legacy verdicts in your own\n * storage and stop supplying them past your policy horizon. Full recipe:\n * the gateway guide (`docs/advanced/gateway.md`).\n */\nexport type PriorDiscovery =\n    /** Adopt `discover` directly: zero round trips. */\n    | { kind: 'modern'; discover: DiscoverResult }\n    /** Known-legacy server: skip the `server/discover` probe and run the plain legacy `initialize` handshake. */\n    | { kind: 'legacy' };\n\n/** The `-32022` UnsupportedProtocolVersion protocol error code (negotiation-phase recognition). */\nconst UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION = -32_022;\n/**\n * Deliberately not probe-recognized in either direction: deployed servers\n * overload `-32001` (the SDK-conventional `Session not found` body on a 2025\n * stateful server), and the spec-assigned `-32020` (`HeaderMismatch`) /\n * `-32021` (`MissingRequiredClientCapability`) are not era evidence — all\n * fall into the conservative legacy default.\n */\nconst NOT_PROBE_RECOGNIZED = new Set([-32_001, -32_020, -32_021]);\n\n/**\n * Classify a single probe outcome. Pure: no I/O, no state — loop-guard and\n * retry state live in the caller.\n */\nexport function classifyProbeOutcome(outcome: ProbeOutcome, context: ProbeClassifierContext): ProbeVerdict {\n    switch (outcome.kind) {\n        case 'result': {\n            return classifyResult(outcome.result, context);\n        }\n        case 'rpc-error': {\n            return classifyRpcError(outcome, context);\n        }\n        case 'http-error': {\n            return classifyHttpError(outcome, context);\n        }\n        case 'network-error': {\n            return classifyNetworkError(outcome.error, context);\n        }\n        case 'auth-required': {\n            // Not era evidence: propagate the auth challenge unchanged so the\n            // caller can run finishAuth() and reconnect — the reconnect probes\n            // again with the token and settles the era with real evidence.\n            // Converting to a legacy fallback here would re-run the auth flow\n            // inside the same connect (a second authorization prompt) and then\n            // handshake an auth-gated modern server as legacy.\n            return { kind: 'error', error: outcome.error };\n        }\n        case 'closed': {\n            if (context.transportKind === 'stdio') {\n                // A stdio child that exits on the unrecognized probe instead of\n                // answering is a legacy signal — the same backward-compatibility\n                // rule as the timeout row below (SDKs like the official Rust one\n                // terminate the server on ANY pre-initialize request).\n                return { kind: 'legacy' };\n            }\n            // On HTTP a mid-probe close is an ambiguous network condition — the\n            // same typed connect error as any probe transport failure.\n            return classifyNetworkError(new Error('Connection closed during the version negotiation probe'), context);\n        }\n        case 'timeout': {\n            if (context.transportKind === 'stdio') {\n                // Per the stdio transport's backward-compatibility rule, a probe\n                // nobody answers within the timeout indicates a legacy server —\n                // fall back to `initialize` (the sibling path runs it on the\n                // session child's fresh pipe; in-place probes reuse the stream).\n                return { kind: 'legacy' };\n            }\n            // On HTTP a deployed server answers, so silence is an outage, not a\n            // legacy signal: keep the typed timeout error (the compatibility\n            // matrix keys the HTTP legacy signal to a 4xx, never to silence).\n            return {\n                kind: 'error',\n                error: new SdkError(SdkErrorCode.RequestTimeout, `Version negotiation probe timed out after ${outcome.timeoutMs}ms`, {\n                    timeout: outcome.timeoutMs\n                })\n            };\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfunction classifyResult(result: unknown, context: ProbeClassifierContext): ProbeVerdict {\n    // The 2026 wire schema carries the spec receiver-side leniency for\n    // `resultType` ('complete'), `ttlMs` (0) and `cacheScope` ('private'), so\n    // routing through the codec is behavior-neutral with the prior public-schema\n    // parse for absent and malformed cache hints (`.catch()` per spec receiver\n    // leniency): a server that omits or malforms them still classifies `modern`.\n    const parsed = codecForVersion(MODERN_WIRE_REVISION).validateResult('server/discover', result);\n    if (!parsed.ok) {\n        // Unrecognized result shape: not modern evidence — conservative legacy fallback.\n        return { kind: 'legacy' };\n    }\n    const supportedVersions = parsed.value.supportedVersions;\n    const overlap = context.clientModernVersions.find(version => supportedVersions.includes(version));\n    if (overlap !== undefined) {\n        return { kind: 'modern', version: overlap, discover: parsed.value };\n    }\n    // A DiscoverResult with no overlap still drives era selection: the legacy\n    // `initialize` fallback when available, otherwise a typed error.\n    if (context.fallbackAvailable) {\n        return { kind: 'legacy' };\n    }\n    return {\n        kind: 'error',\n        error: new UnsupportedProtocolVersionError({ supported: [...supportedVersions], requested: context.requestedVersion })\n    };\n}\n\nfunction classifyRpcError(outcome: { code: number; message: string; data?: unknown }, context: ProbeClassifierContext): ProbeVerdict {\n    const { code, message, data } = outcome;\n\n    if (code === UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION) {\n        const supported = parseSupportedList(data);\n        if (supported === undefined) {\n            // -32022 without a valid data.supported list is not actionable modern evidence.\n            return { kind: 'legacy' };\n        }\n        const requested = parseRequested(data) ?? context.requestedVersion;\n        const error = new UnsupportedProtocolVersionError({ supported, requested }, message);\n        const supportedModern = modernProtocolVersions(supported);\n        const mutual = context.clientModernVersions.find(version => supportedModern.includes(version));\n        if (mutual !== undefined) {\n            // Mutual modern version: spec-mandated select-and-continue — never\n            // fall back to initialize here.\n            return { kind: 'corrective', version: mutual, error };\n        }\n        if (supportedModern.length > 0) {\n            // Disjoint-but-modern list: typed error, never initialize.\n            return { kind: 'error', error };\n        }\n        // Legacy-only list: definitive legacy signal (typed error for a modern-only client).\n        return context.fallbackAvailable ? { kind: 'legacy' } : { kind: 'error', error };\n    }\n\n    if (NOT_PROBE_RECOGNIZED.has(code)) {\n        return { kind: 'legacy' };\n    }\n\n    // Everything else — -32601, the deployed -32000 literals/free-text, code 0,\n    // any unrecognized code — is a legacy signal or the conservative default.\n    return { kind: 'legacy' };\n}\n\nfunction classifyHttpError(outcome: { status: number; body?: string; statusText?: string }, context: ProbeClassifierContext): ProbeVerdict {\n    // Auth statuses are never era evidence, and a 401/403 body is the auth\n    // layer's, not the server/discover handler's — this row ranks above the\n    // JSON-RPC body parse. Parallel to the auth-required row: a typed failure\n    // naming the status (response text on `data.text`), never a legacy\n    // fallback. The codes are the auth ones, NOT EraNegotiationFailed: hosts\n    // key era-recovery recipes (e.g. the gateway guide's cached-verdict flow)\n    // on EraNegotiationFailed, and an auth wall must never enter era recovery\n    // — persisting a legacy verdict for it would recreate the silent-legacy\n    // bug at the fleet level.\n    if (outcome.status === 401 || outcome.status === 403) {\n        const isDenial = outcome.status === 403;\n        return {\n            kind: 'error',\n            error: new SdkHttpError(\n                isDenial ? SdkErrorCode.ClientHttpForbidden : SdkErrorCode.ClientHttpAuthentication,\n                `Version negotiation failed: ${isDenial ? 'the server denied access (HTTP 403)' : 'the server requires authorization (HTTP 401)'}`,\n                {\n                    status: outcome.status,\n                    statusText: outcome.statusText,\n                    text: outcome.body\n                }\n            )\n        };\n    }\n    if (outcome.status >= 500) {\n        // A server failure is not era evidence, whatever the body says — this\n        // row too ranks above the JSON-RPC body parse (a 5xx body is the\n        // infrastructure's: a mid-deploy gateway's JSON error page, a crashed\n        // handler's -32603, neither a server/discover verdict). The spec keys\n        // the HTTP legacy signal to client-error rejections (a 2025 server\n        // answers the unknown probe 4xx), never to 5xx.\n        return {\n            kind: 'error',\n            error: new SdkHttpError(\n                SdkErrorCode.EraNegotiationFailed,\n                `Version negotiation failed: the server answered the probe with HTTP ${outcome.status}`,\n                {\n                    status: outcome.status,\n                    statusText: outcome.statusText,\n                    text: outcome.body\n                }\n            )\n        };\n    }\n    // HTTP-rejected probes carry their JSON-RPC error in the response body — classify it like an in-band error.\n    const rpcError = parseJsonRpcErrorBody(outcome.body);\n    if (rpcError !== undefined) {\n        return classifyRpcError(rpcError, context);\n    }\n    // Unparseable or unrecognized 4xx rejection: conservative legacy fallback.\n    // With the auth and 5xx rows above, this row's legacy set now equals the\n    // spec-licensed set exactly — the 4xx a deployed 2025 server answers a\n    // request it does not recognize.\n    return { kind: 'legacy' };\n}\n\nfunction classifyNetworkError(error: unknown, context: ProbeClassifierContext): ProbeVerdict {\n    if (context.environment === 'browser' && isOpaqueFetchTypeError(error)) {\n        // A browser CORS-preflight rejection against a deployed 2025 server is\n        // an opaque TypeError. The legacy fallback also preflights (its JSON\n        // Content-Type is non-simple), but carries only the pre-2026 headers a\n        // deployed server's CORS allowlist already covers — so it can proceed\n        // where the probe's 2026 headers could not.\n        return { kind: 'legacy' };\n    }\n    return {\n        kind: 'error',\n        error: new SdkError(SdkErrorCode.EraNegotiationFailed, `Version negotiation probe failed: ${describeError(error)}`, {\n            cause: error\n        })\n    };\n}\n\nfunction isOpaqueFetchTypeError(error: unknown): boolean {\n    // Cross-realm safe: a bundled or sandboxed fetch may not share this realm's TypeError identity.\n    return error instanceof TypeError || (error instanceof Error && error.name === 'TypeError');\n}\n\nfunction describeError(error: unknown): string {\n    return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);\n}\n\nfunction parseSupportedList(data: unknown): string[] | undefined {\n    if (typeof data !== 'object' || data === null) return undefined;\n    const supported = (data as { supported?: unknown }).supported;\n    if (!Array.isArray(supported) || supported.length === 0 || !supported.every(v => typeof v === 'string')) {\n        return undefined;\n    }\n    return supported as string[];\n}\n\nfunction parseRequested(data: unknown): string | undefined {\n    if (typeof data !== 'object' || data === null) return undefined;\n    const requested = (data as { requested?: unknown }).requested;\n    return typeof requested === 'string' ? requested : undefined;\n}\n\nfunction parseJsonRpcErrorBody(body: string | undefined): { code: number; message: string; data?: unknown } | undefined {\n    if (body === undefined || body === '') return undefined;\n    let parsed: unknown;\n    try {\n        parsed = JSON.parse(body);\n    } catch {\n        return undefined;\n    }\n    if (typeof parsed !== 'object' || parsed === null) return undefined;\n    const error = (parsed as { error?: unknown }).error;\n    if (typeof error !== 'object' || error === null) return undefined;\n    const { code, message, data } = error as { code?: unknown; message?: unknown; data?: unknown };\n    if (typeof code !== 'number') return undefined;\n    return { code, message: typeof message === 'string' ? message : '', data };\n}\n", "/**\n * Connect-time protocol version negotiation (opt-in via\n * `ClientOptions.versionNegotiation`): the option surface, the probe window (a\n * raw transport exchange run before the Protocol machinery attaches), and the\n * negotiation engine driving the pure {@linkcode classifyProbeOutcome} classifier.\n *\n * Invariants: the probe uses string ids and consumes no Protocol message ids, so\n * a legacy fallback's `initialize` is byte-equivalent to a plain legacy connect;\n * the transport's protocol-version slot is never mutated during negotiation\n * (probe headers derive from the probe message body) and is set exactly once\n * after a modern resolution; Governs timeout re-sends only — the spec-mandated\n     * `-32022` corrective continuation (select-and-continue with a mutual\n     * version) is a separate negotiation step and is never counted against\n     * `maxRetries`.\n     *\n     * @default 0 (no retries)\n     */\n    maxRetries?: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Negotiation mode:\n *\n * - `'legacy'` — no negotiation: the plain 2025 connect sequence, byte-identical\n *   to a client without this option.\n * - `'auto'` — probe with `server/discover` at connect; conservative fallback to\n *   the plain legacy `initialize` handshake unless the outcome is definitive\n *   modern evidence. No fallback — anything else\n *   fails loudly with a typed error.\n */\nexport type VersionNegotiationMode = 'legacy' | 'auto' | { pin: string };\n\n/**\n * Opt-in protocol version negotiation, configured on\n * `ClientOptions.versionNegotiation`.\n */\nexport interface VersionNegotiationOptions {\n    /**\n     * @default 'legacy'\n     */\n    mode?: VersionNegotiationMode;\n\n    /**\n     * Probe timeout/retry policy (only consulted by the probing modes).\n     */\n    probe?: VersionNegotiationProbeOptions;\n}\n\n/**\n * The default mode when `versionNegotiation` (or its `mode`) is absent;\n * changing the default later is a flip of this single line.\n */\nconst DEFAULT_VERSION_NEGOTIATION_MODE: VersionNegotiationMode = 'legacy';\n\n/** A fully resolved negotiation plan for one `connect()` call. */\nexport type ResolvedVersionNegotiation =\n    | { kind: 'legacy' }\n    | {\n          kind: 'auto';\n          /** Modern versions this client offers, in preference order (never empty). */\n          modernVersions: string[];\n          /** Whether this client can fall back to the legacy `initialize` handshake. */\n          fallbackAvailable: boolean;\n          probe: VersionNegotiationProbeOptions;\n      }\n    | { kind: 'pin'; version: string; probe: VersionNegotiationProbeOptions };\n\n/**\n * Resolve the negotiation options into a per-connect plan. The raw (not\n * defaulted) `supportedProtocolVersions` option supplies the modern offer list;\n * a list without any legacy version makes this a modern-only client (no fallback).\n */\nexport function resolveVersionNegotiation(\n    options: VersionNegotiationOptions | undefined,\n    supportedProtocolVersionsOption: readonly string[] | undefined\n): ResolvedVersionNegotiation {\n    const mode = options?.mode ?? 'browser' : 'node';\n}\n\n/**\n * Detect the transport class for the transport-aware timeout and closed verdicts (see\n * {@linkcode ProbeTransportKind}). The stdio child-process transport is\n * recognized structurally (`stderr`/`pid` accessors, no `instanceof` — safe\n * across bundles); everything else is treated like HTTP.\n */\nexport function detectProbeTransportKind(transport: Transport): ProbeTransportKind {\n    return 'stderr' in transport && 'pid' in transport ? 'stdio' : 'http';\n}\n\n/** Raw reply from one probe exchange, before normalization. */\ntype RawProbeReply =\n    | { kind: 'response'; result?: unknown; error?: { code: number; message: string; data?: unknown } }\n    | { kind: 'send-error'; error: unknown }\n    | { kind: 'closed' }\n    | { kind: 'timeout' };\n\n/**\n * Temporary ownership of a raw transport for the negotiation exchange, before\n * the Protocol machinery attaches. `open()` installs the window's handlers and\n * starts the transport; `release()` detaches them and arms a one-shot `start()`\n * pass-through so the subsequent Protocol connect (which always starts its\n * transport) takes over the already-started channel without a double-start error.\n *\n * Handlers a caller pre-set on the transport before `connect()` are saved on\n * open and restored on detach, so `Protocol.connect()` finds and chains them\n * exactly as it would on a plain (non-negotiating) connect. Error and close\n * events are forwarded to the saved handlers during the window, so negotiation\n * does not change what a pre-attached observer sees of the transport\n * lifecycle. (Inbound messages are deliberately NOT forwarded — the window's\n * drop-guard is a module invariant, and the probe reply has no plain-connect\n * counterpart; a pre-set `onmessage` is restored at detach and chained by\n * `Protocol.connect()` like the others.)\n */\nclass ProbeWindow {\n    private _pending: { id: string; resolve: (reply: RawProbeReply) => void } | undefined;\n    private _probeCounter = 0;\n    private readonly _savedOnMessage: Transport['onmessage'];\n    private readonly _savedOnError: Transport['onerror'];\n    private readonly _savedOnClose: Transport['onclose'];\n    private _closeDelivered = false;\n\n    private constructor(private readonly _transport: Transport) {\n        this._savedOnMessage = _transport.onmessage;\n        this._savedOnError = _transport.onerror;\n        this._savedOnClose = _transport.onclose;\n    }\n\n    static async open(transport: Transport): Promise<ProbeWindow> {\n        const window = new ProbeWindow(transport);\n        transport.onmessage = message => {\n            const pending = window._pending;\n            if (\n                pending !== undefined &&\n                (isJSONRPCResultResponse(message) || isJSONRPCErrorResponse(message)) &&\n                message.id === pending.id\n            ) {\n                window._pending = undefined;\n                if (isJSONRPCResultResponse(message)) {\n                    pending.resolve({ kind: 'response', result: message.result });\n                } else {\n                    pending.resolve({ kind: 'response', error: message.error });\n                }\n                return;\n            }\n            // Probe-window guard: drop everything else with zero bytes written back (see module doc).\n        };\n        transport.onerror = error => {\n            // Out-of-band transport errors are not necessarily fatal; the probe\n            // resolves via a send failure, the close signal, or the timeout.\n            window._savedOnError?.(error);\n        };\n        transport.onclose = () => {\n            const pending = window._pending;\n            if (pending !== undefined) {\n                window._pending = undefined;\n                pending.resolve({ kind: 'closed' });\n            }\n            // Forward exactly once: after a mid-window close is delivered, the\n            // restored handler must not re-deliver it when cleanup paths call\n            // `transport.close()` again.\n            window._closeDelivered = true;\n            window._savedOnClose?.();\n        };\n        try {\n            await transport.start();\n        } catch (error) {\n            window.detach();\n            throw error;\n        }\n        return window;\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * Send one probe request and await its reply. Probe ids are strings, so they\n     * never collide with Protocol's numeric ids (e.g. on a shared stdio pipe).\n     */\n    async exchange(buildRequest: (id: string) => JSONRPCRequest, timeoutMs: number): Promise<RawProbeReply> {\n        const id = `server-discover-probe-${++this._probeCounter}`;\n        return new Promise<RawProbeReply>(resolve => {\n            let settled = false;\n            const settle = (reply: RawProbeReply) => {\n                if (settled) return;\n                settled = true;\n                clearTimeout(timer);\n                if (this._pending?.id === id) {\n                    this._pending = undefined;\n                }\n                resolve(reply);\n            };\n            const timer = setTimeout(() => settle({ kind: 'timeout' }), timeoutMs);\n            this._pending = { id, resolve: settle };\n            this._transport.send(buildRequest(id)).catch((error: unknown) => settle({ kind: 'send-error', error }));\n        });\n    }\n\n    /** Detach the window's handlers, restoring any the caller pre-set, leaving the transport's own `start` untouched. */\n    detach(): void {\n        this._pending = undefined;\n        this._transport.onmessage = this._savedOnMessage;\n        this._transport.onerror = this._savedOnError;\n        if (this._closeDelivered && this._savedOnClose !== undefined) {\n            // The forwarded mid-window close is spent — the caller's cleanup\n            // close() must not re-deliver it — but the slot must not be emptied\n            // either: the caller still owns the transport, and its observer must\n            // keep seeing later closes. The skip is scoped to the cleanup close\n            // via disarmSpentCloseGuard(): transports whose close() re-fires\n            // onclose (HTTP) consume it there; transports that never re-fire\n            // (stdio: onclose comes only from the child's close event, which\n            // already happened) would otherwise leave it armed to swallow the\n            // NEXT genuine close after a restart.\n            const saved = this._savedOnClose;\n            const transport = this._transport;\n            let spent = false;\n            const wrapper = () => {\n                if (!spent) {\n                    spent = true;\n                    return;\n                }\n                saved();\n            };\n            transport.onclose = wrapper;\n            pendingSpentCloseGuards.set(transport, () => {\n                // Restore by identity — never clobber a handler the caller\n                // replaced in the meantime.\n                if (transport.onclose === wrapper) {\n                    transport.onclose = saved;\n                }\n            });\n        } else {\n            this._transport.onclose = this._savedOnClose;\n
